prompt:
Evaluation ticket (authored for this study; not an existing ProcLease issue).

`proclease list` can only be widened with `--all`. Callers that want, for example, only failed jobs must filter JSON themselves. Add a repeatable `--state <STATE>` filter to `list`.

Acceptance criteria:
1. `list --state <STATE>` accepts exactly the nine lifecycle state names used in JSON `state` values: `starting`, `running`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `expired`, `exited`, `failed`, `interrupted`, `unknown` (lowercase, exact). Each occurrence takes one name. Comma-separated lists, other spellings or case, and aliases such as `active` or `unverified` fail with a nonzero exit status and print no job list. Repeating a name is allowed and has no extra effect.
2. A job matches when its displayed state equals any requested name (OR across repeated options). The displayed state is the state `list` reports now, after the existing supervisor observation: a `running` record whose supervisor endpoint is unreachable is shown, and matched, as `unknown`.
3. Filtering happens before the default recent-finished window. Without `--all`, matching active and unverified jobs are always shown, and the five most recently finished matching jobs stay visible for 30 seconds under the existing rules. With `--all`, every matching retained job is shown.
4. Output order, fields and the JSON envelope are the same as today, restricted to matching jobs, in human and JSON output and with `--resources`. Scan warnings (for example an unreadable job record) are still reported when filtering, because the state of such a record is unknown.
5. Without `--state`, `list` output is unchanged. `watch` is unchanged.
6. The filter only reads: it adds no lease renewal, signal or record write. The opportunistic history collection that every `list` already performs is unchanged.
7. Help text lists the accepted values. README `list` usage documents the option and that it matches the displayed state.
8. Integration tests in tests/lifecycle.rs cover criteria 1 to 6 using seeded job records rather than timing-sensitive live processes.

Scope: src/, tests/ and README.md only. Do not change Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, dependencies, the shared skill, website, release or packaging files. Tests must be deterministic, honour PROCLEASE_TEST_ROOT like the existing fixtures and stop anything they start. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` must pass with CARGO_TARGET_DIR and PROCLEASE_TEST_ROOT set outside the repository.
common_acceptance: cargo test passes (full suite, run by the grader with the case environment)
Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock unchanged; no new dependencies
changed paths are within allowed_paths; anything else is an out-of-scope change
no commits, pushes, tags, releases, website, packaging or skill changes; working-tree changes only
tests are deterministic, honour PROCLEASE_TEST_ROOT and stop every process they start

fatal.definition: The state does not compile, or no usable binary can be produced from it.
fatal.counting: One fatal flag per state, ranked with blockers. Hidden checks are then not_run and are NOT counted as separate defects.

severity.blocker: A stated safety invariant is violated: protected, active, unverified or retention-protected history deleted; a dry run or invalid input deletes; a read-only path writes, renews or signals; symlink refusal bypassed; environment values exposed; a mismatched keyed retry reused; or the requested feature is absent or unusable.
severity.major: A stated acceptance criterion fails in an ordinary scenario: wrong selection, window, order, count or path; an unchanged-behavior regression; an invalid value accepted with wrong behavior; full cargo test fails; required tests missing for a whole criterion.
severity.minor: An edge-case, message, envelope, help or README deviation; fmt or clippy failure; weak but present tests; nonzero required but a different nonzero class returned.

causal_dedup: Hidden-check severities are frozen in the grader declaration. Each failing causal group counts as one defect at the highest severity among its non-dependent failing checks.
A failing check whose declared depends_on check also failed is a dependent symptom and does not count.
Groups sharing one root cause are merged into one defect when the blind grader cites the single code location responsible; the merged defect takes the highest severity.
If the feature is absent or unusable, every positive check failure collapses into one blocker. Safety and compatibility checks still count separately when they fail.
One unique_issue_id is kept for the same causal issue across I, A, B and C on a task, so corrections and regressions can be tracked.

defect_record.reproduction: A command sequence with fixture or a cited code path plus the input that reaches it. A model opinion without one is recorded as unconfirmed and never counted.

maintainability_anchors.0: Unmaintainable: logic conflicts with existing structure, misleading names or comments, dead or duplicated code paths that will diverge.
maintainability_anchors.1: Poor: works locally but is placed or duplicated inconsistently with existing helpers; tests brittle (timing, live processes) or missing.
maintainability_anchors.2: Adequate: follows the existing structure with some duplication, unclear edges or thin tests or docs.
maintainability_anchors.3: Good: idiomatic and localized, reuses existing helpers, deterministic tests cover the criteria, docs accurate.
maintainability_anchors.4: Excellent: minimal and clear, well-factored, precise deterministic tests, exact docs, nothing superfluous.
